title: Heterogeneous-device conductor for staggered rendezvous and attention-fusion routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Redwood's current multi-GPU conductor optimizes for homogeneous device sets and synchronized NCCL windows. For mixed-device clusters (different GPU generations, NVLink topologies, or asymmetric bandwidth between pipeline stages) the scheduler either serializes communications conservatively or over-parallelizes NCCL launches, causing increased latency and lowered throughput for prefill/decode workloads.

Goal:
Design and implement a "conductor" layer that can: (1) observe device-level bandwidth/latency characteristics at runtime, (2) create staggered rendezvous windows to maximize NCCL overlap without increasing tail latencies, (3) route attention-prefill work to fused attention kernels when beneficial, and (4) remain compatible with existing tensor/pipeline parallel layouts and autoscaling policies.

Approach:
- Runtime probing: lightweight microbenchmarks at job start (and opportunistic re-probes) to build an affinity matrix for NVLink/NCCL performance between device pairs.
- Rendezvous planner: generate per-step communication schedules that stagger collective roots to avoid hot-spoting on limited links; schedule windows according to observed bandwidth and the size of KV/activation transfers.
- Opportunistic NCCL coalescing: where topology and timing permit, merge small collectives into batched NCCL ops; otherwise, issue staggered smaller collectives timed to hide overlap with local compute.
- Attention fusion routing: use kernel-selection heuristics to route certain attention patterns (short sequence prefill, multiquery heads) to our fused attention kernel on capable devices while routing fallback kernels to others; ensure KV cache consistency across mixed kernels.
- Prefill/Decode phase differentiation: adopt different scheduling policies for prefill (large bulk KV transfers, more tolerant to batching) vs decode (low-latency streaming with tight SLO).
- Safety and fallbacks: add a deterministic fallback path that disables staggering and fusion when any device reports driver/kernel incompatibility or if error rates increase beyond threshold.

Success metrics:
- 15% reduction in median per-request latency for heterogeneous clusters on standard prefill+decode traces.
- 10–25% throughput improvement for high-concurrency workloads on mixed-node NVLink topologies.
- No regressions >5% in tail latency (P95/P99) across homogeneous clusters.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Additional probing cost at job start (mitigated via sampling and cached topology profiles).
- Complexity of correctness across mixed attention kernels (mitigated via strong integration tests and KV consistency checks).
- Potential interaction with Dedicated autoscaler; need to ensure staging doesn't cause oscillation in load signals.

Notes:
Keep changes modular: conductor planner + kernel router should be pluggable components to keep rollouts (canary A/B) straightforward.

2026-03-08 | Marco Liu: Implemented microprobe harness and ran on mixed 3090+A100 cluster. Preliminary results: 18% median latency improvement on prefill-heavy trace, but P99 regressed by 6% under high contention. Added thresholded smoothing to planner.
2026-03-10 | SRE - Tom Becker: Noted that probing increases job start time by ~80ms for 8-GPU jobs; recommended probe batching and caching profiles per node image.

2026-03-12 | Marco Liu: Opened prototype PR with conductor core + kernel router: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428. Running integration e2e on our perf cluster (job 2026-03-12-ENG70123).

acceptance_criteria: Conductor implements runtime probing and builds an affinity matrix available to the scheduler.
Planner produces staggered rendezvous schedules that can be enabled per-job and per-phase (prefill vs decode).
Kernel router can select fused attention on capable devices while falling back safely on others with KV consistency verified in tests.
Bench results: >=15% median latency improvement on at least two mixed-topology traces without >5% P99 regressions on homogeneous baselines.
Feature gated behind runtime.scheduler.heterogeneous_conductor flag and rollout plan documented (canary steps, metrics to monitor).
